title: Changing flow with break, continue, return, and goto
hook: Jump statements move execution to a different place in your code. You will use break, continue, and return constantly. goto is legal but rare — except goto case in a classic switch, which is the honest way to fall through.

blocks.text: A **jump statement** transfers control away from the current line. **break** exits the innermost loop or switch. **continue** skips to the next iteration of a loop. **return** exits the current method and optionally provides a value. **goto** jumps to a label in the same method — or to another case in a switch via goto case. These are not errors or hacks; they are first-class language features with clear rules.

entries.plainDefinition: Exits the innermost enclosing switch, loop, or labeled statement immediately.
entries.example: break; inside a switch case prevents fall-through to the next case.

entries.plainDefinition: Skips the rest of the current loop iteration and moves to the next one.
entries.example: continue; after logging a bad SQS message skips Process() for that message.

entries.plainDefinition: The only legal way to fall through between switch cases in C#. Jumps execution to another case label.
entries.example: goto case 404; after handling a 500 status code.

sections.heading: Why jumps beat deeply nested ifs

blocks.text: In an SQS batch loop, continue on a poison payload after logging is clearer than three levels of nested if. return early from a method when validation fails instead of wrapping the rest in else blocks. break out of a search loop when you find the target. These patterns keep code flat and readable. Reserve goto for goto case in switches — unstructured goto across methods is never legal.

blocks.title: return and process exit codes
blocks.body: return from Main or a top-level program with an int sets the process exit code. return 0 means success; non-zero signals failure to scripts and orchestrators.

items.title: break
items.body: Leaves the nearest switch or loop. Execution continues at the statement after the closing brace.

items.title: continue
items.body: Skips to the loop condition check (while/for) or the next MoveNext (foreach).

items.title: return
items.body: Exits the entire method. No code after return in that method runs.

items.title: goto label / goto case
items.body: Jumps to a label in the same method, or to a switch case label.

diagram.title: Jump targets in a loop
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  A[Loop body start] --> B{Bad message?}
  B -->|Yes| C[continue — skip to next iteration]
  B -->|No| D[Process message]
  D --> E{Batch done?}
  E -->|No| A
  E -->|Yes| F[break — exit loop]
  F --> G[return 0 — exit method]

snippet.label: continue on bad messages; return a code
snippet.explanation: continue skips the rest of the current iteration. return exits the method entirely. In a top-level program, return 0 sets the process exit code.

snippet.label: goto case for explicit switch fall-through
snippet.explanation: Stacked case 1: case 2: without code between is multiple labels on one section — not statement fall-through. Statement fall-through still needs goto case.

snippet.label: Early return for validation
snippet.explanation: Early return flattens validation logic. Each failure path exits immediately with a distinct code.

blocks.title: C# vs JavaScript/TypeScript jumps
rows: Same — but return in forEach only exits callback
Legal with labels; goto case in switch
Falls through by default in JS

blocks.title: Top pitfalls
blocks.body: Expecting C-style implicit switch fall-through. Using goto across try/finally blocks — the compiler forbids jumping out of a finally. Returning from a void lambda expecting it to exit the outer method — it only exits the lambda (delegates covered later). Using break outside a loop or switch — compile error.

interviewTakeaways: break and continue affect the nearest loop or switch.
return from Main or top-level sets the process exit code when the type is int.
goto is legal; cite goto case if asked for a legitimate use.
Early return beats deeply nested else chains for validation.
commonPitfalls: Using goto across try/finally and fighting the compiler.
Returning from a void lambda by habit of JS return in forEach — different construct (delegates later).
Using break to exit multiple nested loops — it only exits the innermost one.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Same words, same idea. JavaScript labeled statements exist but are rare; C# labels are mainly for goto. JavaScript switch fall-through is the default; C# forbids it without goto case.
